Consider the following PR description:
FindStartOfPreviousWord only searches for tabs instead of spaces

#### Description

The `FindStartOfPreviousWord` function is not working correctly when text contains spaces. It appears to only search for tab characters instead of space characters, causing it to return 0 when there are actual word boundaries marked by spaces.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/c-bata/go-prompt"
)

func main() {
    // Create a document with space-separated words
    doc := &prompt.Document{
        Text:   "hello world test",
        cursor: 16, // Position at end
    }
    
    // This should find the start of "test" (position 12)
    // but returns 0 instead
    pos := doc.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
    fmt.Printf("Expected: 12, Got: %d\n", pos)
    
    // Another example
    doc2 := &prompt.Document{
        Text:   "apple banana",
        cursor: 12, // Position at end  
    }
    
    // This should find the start of "banana" (position 6)
    // but returns 0 instead
    pos2 := doc2.FindStartOfPreviousWord()
    fmt.Printf("Expected: 6, Got: %d\n", pos2)
}
```

The function works fine with tab-separated words but fails completely with space-separated words, which is the more common use case.
</pr_description>
